history.summary: A freehold D19 unit 560m from the future CRL Serangoon North station, listed at $1,206 psf — a striking ~20% below the project's $1,509 URA median. The discount plus a confirmed CRL catalyst is the thesis, but the 829 sqft '1BR' label is anomalous and the 26-transaction series is thin.
history.rating_rationale: Listed PSF $1,206 is ~20% under the URA median of $1,509 — a large, genuine discount on a freehold asset. The standout catalyst is the future Cross Island Line station 560m away (~2030), which historically drives 10-20% uplift within 500-600m. Freehold tenure removes lease-decay risk over the hold. Two caveats temper this to Buy rather than Strong Buy: the 829 sqft '1BR' classification is unusual (likely a large 1BR+study or a mislabel — the size pulls PSF down and may not be a true 1-bedder, affecting the comp), and the 26-txn URA series makes the 5.9%/yr rate moderately reliable only. Sub-$1M-area freehold quantum keeps it liquid.
red_flags: 829 sqft for a '1BR' is anomalous — verify actual layout/classification, the low PSF may partly reflect an oversized unit
Thin 26-transaction URA series — appreciation rate less reliable
Below-median listing PSF — confirm no defect/orientation issue behind the discount
catalysts: Future CRL Serangoon North MRT 560m away (~2030) — strong proximity uplift
Freehold tenure premium in a leasehold-heavy district
~20% discount to project URA median offers margin of safety

history.summary: The unit is genuinely below comparable 2-BR-sized transactions, but a tiny 103-unit project, a weak 2.9% yield and a soft long-dated catalyst keep this short of a Buy despite the real discount.
history.rating_rationale: Asking $1,206 psf for 829 sqft (a 2-BR footprint, not a true 1-BR) compares against recent 883 sqft 2-BR transactions at $1,445-$1,586 psf and a 12-month project avg of ~$1,486 psf — so the discount is real and web-verified, supporting the very_low_psf flag and -28.0% age-adj premium. Freehold and D19 (OCR, the strongest forward region under v3.4) are positives. But two factors hold it at Neutral: (1) only 103 units means thin resale/rental liquidity and lumpy exit, and (2) the 2.9% gross yield is the weakest of the cohort. With psf_cohort_txns=2 and only 26 appreciation txns, the data depth is modest. The value is there but the liquidity and income case is not strong enough to clear the Buy bar.
red_flags: Tiny 103-unit development — shallow resale market and lumpy, hard-to-time exits over a 5-7yr hold
2.9% gross yield is weak — poor cashflow coverage for an investment hold
psf_cohort_txns=2 and only 26 appreciation txns — thinnest appreciation base in the cohort
Not MRT-fronting today; nearest is bus-dependent until CRL stations open
$1,000,000 asking sits at the round-number ceiling with limited negotiation headroom signalled
catalysts: Verified discount to comparable 2-BR-sized transactions ($1,206 vs $1,445-$1,586 psf)
Freehold tenure in OCR D19 (downside floor; OCR is the best forward region per v3.4)
Future Cross Island Line connectivity in the Serangoon North / Hougang corridor (long-dated, ~2030+)
